newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds mixed, eye on EBR and sterling.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds mixed, eye on EBR and sterling.

text.p: Irish government bonds were mixed in quiet trade on Monday as the market awaited Irish Exchequer Borrowing Requirement (EBR) data and continued to monitor currency market movements, dealers said.

"Irish bonds enjoyed a little bounce in the morning but I'd be very cautious about making any predictions for the week. The EBR figures (due at 1630 GMT) should show a deficit of about 150 million Irish pounds for October," one dealer said.
By 1552 GMT the eight percent bond due 2000 was 20p stronger at 105.75 to yield 6.22 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 was off ten pence at 106.65 to yield 6.92.
The eight percent bond due 2015 was at 109.40, a rise of five pence.
"The Irish central bank seems to be doing its best to keep the Irish pound above 1.00 sterling," one dealer said.
Dealers said German bunds had started the week well and in late afternoon Irish 10-year bond yields were at 100 basis points over bunds.
They said the UK and Irish interest rate outlook remained a focus.
"Tax cuts in the UK Budget could trigger further UK rate rises if consumer spending goes up," one dealer said.

"I wouldn't rule out a short-term interest rise in Ireland either. The credit numbers on Thursday will be interesting for the market," he added. Ireland's central bank releases September credit growth data at 1630 GMT on Thursday.

Dealers said the bond market would be focusing on select batches of data this week. The Bank of England inflation report, the CBI survey, U.S. consumer credit and money supply figures were mentioned by dealers.
